title: Relative derived tensor under a faithfully flat extension of the coefficient algebra
statement:
Let $R\to A\to B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, with $A\to B$ faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Use unbounded derived categories of modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and derived tensors computed by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Let $K\in D(A)$ be arbitrary. The exact functor $-\otimes_A B$ applied termwise to any representing $A$-complex computes $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$. For every degree-zero $R$-module $N$, give $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$ its $A$-action on the $K$ factor. There is a natural isomorphism in $D(B)$
$$ (K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\ \cong\ (K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N. $$
Naturality is in $K\in D(A)$ and in $R$-module maps of $N$. For every pair of integers $a\le b$, $K$, restricted to $R$, has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ if and only if $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$, restricted to $R$, has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Here Tor amplitude over $R$ means vanishing of $H^i(-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)$ for all degree-zero $R$-modules $N$ and all $i\notin[a,b]$. Neither $A$ nor $B$ is assumed flat over $R$, and no boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: Write T(C)=C\otimes_A B termwise. Faithful flatness implies that T is exact. The exact-functor cohomology lemma gives H^i(T(C))\cong H^i(C)\otimes_A B naturally, for every unbounded C, hence T preserves quasi-isomorphisms. To compare with derived extension, take an A-K-flat resolution P\to C. Apply clause (2) of the derived-second-factor tensor lemma with base ring A, coefficient algebra B and fixed complex B[0]: C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B is represented by P\otimes_A B. The quasi-isomorphism T(P)\to T(C) identifies this with T(C) in D(B). Thus every representative computes derived extension, including any complex appearing below.

source.place: Tag 0DJF (lemma-no-change-tor-amplitude), proof; mixed derived tensor construction Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change) and K-flat resolutions Tag 06Y4 (lemma-K-flat-resolution).

proof.text: Choose an arbitrary A-complex C representing K and an R-K-flat resolution F\to N[0], which exists with no boundedness condition. Clause (2) of the derived-second-factor tensor lemma, with fixed coefficient complex C, computes N\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K in D(A) by Tot(F\otimes_R C). The signed symmetry f\otimes c\mapsto(-1)^{pq}c\otimes f in bidegree (p,q) identifies this with U=Tot(C\otimes_R F). The mixed-tensor restriction comparison identifies its underlying R-complex with the ordinary total tensor, so U represents K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N with precisely the A-action on C. Applying the same construction to T(C) gives V=Tot(T(C)\otimes_R F), representing (K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N in D(B).

source.place: Tag 0DJF (lemma-no-change-tor-amplitude), proof; mixed derived tensor construction Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change) and K-flat resolutions Tag 06Y4 (lemma-K-flat-resolution).

proof.text: Apply the mixed-total-tensor scalar-extension isomorphism to R\to A\to B, Q=C and the chosen F. Using M\otimes_A(A\otimes_R E)\cong M\otimes_R E from the mixed-tensor definition, and commuting the degree-zero B factor, it is the B-linear chain isomorphism T(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}V whose diagonal formula is (c\otimes f)\otimes b\mapsto(c\otimes b)\otimes f. Its inverse sends (c\otimes b)\otimes f to (c\otimes f)\otimes b. Steps 1 and 2 identify its source and target with the two derived objects in the statement; localization therefore gives the required isomorphism in D(B). This uses the full chain isomorphism, not merely isomorphisms on cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0DJF (lemma-no-change-tor-amplitude), proof; mixed derived tensor construction Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change) and K-flat resolutions Tag 06Y4 (lemma-K-flat-resolution).

proof.text: The diagonal formula of step 3 commutes with maps C\to C' and F\to F': both routes send (c\otimes f)\otimes b to (u(c)\otimes b)\otimes v(f). For fixed F, mixed K-flat tensor preserves every quasi-isomorphism in C, and T does so by step 1. The localization universal property thus descends these natural squares to all K-morphisms in D(A), including inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. For fixed C, regard T(U) and V as functors of the R-complex F. Clause (2) of the derived-second-factor tensor lemma supplies their canonical K-flat computation, and clause (1), equivalently mixed K-flat invariance, ensures independence of the resolution F\to N[0]. Deriving the natural chain comparison gives the corresponding natural transformation in D(R); its components are isomorphisms since they are computed by step 3 on each K-flat resolution. This is the universal left-derived-functor comparison, so its squares are the derived squares in N. Clause (3) of the same lemma identifies changes of the fixed coefficient complex with the chain maps 1_F\otimes u; hence the two naturalities agree. Restrict the R-derived variable to degree-zero modules to obtain the stated naturality in module maps N\to N'.

source.place: Tag 0DJF (lemma-no-change-tor-amplitude), proof; mixed derived tensor construction Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change) and K-flat resolutions Tag 06Y4 (lemma-K-flat-resolution).

proof.text: Apply the exact-functor cohomology comparison of step 1 to U and the chain isomorphism T(U)\cong V of step 3. In every integer degree i this gives H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)\otimes_A B\cong H^i((K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N). The left cohomology is an A-module because U is an A-complex; the right is a B-module. Thus all scalar actions needed for faithful-flat detection are the ones already specified, without assuming A or B flat over R.

source.place: Tag 0DJF (lemma-no-change-tor-amplitude), proof; mixed derived tensor construction Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change) and K-flat resolutions Tag 06Y4 (lemma-K-flat-resolution).

proof.text: Fix a\le b. If K has R-Tor amplitude in [a,b], each left cohomology module in step 5 is zero for every R-module N and i\notin[a,b], so its tensor with B and hence the right cohomology vanish. Conversely, if all those right cohomology groups vanish, step 5 and faithful-flat tensor detection (with base A, faithfully flat module B and test module H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)) imply that each left cohomology module is zero. Quantifying over N and i\notin[a,b] is exactly the two Tor-amplitude conditions. Forgetting to R does not change whether a cohomology module is zero.
